claims.text: NiCoFeCr is a high-entropy alloy suitable for use as a thin interfacial layer in HEA multilayers.
Introducing a thin NiCoFeCr layer with a coherent interface can facilitate a transition between diffusion-mediated and dislocation-mediated creep.
The proposed transition occurs in HEA multilayers at high temperatures.
The relevant initial materials are as-deposited or annealed NiCoFeCr HEA multilayer coatings.
The intervention is the introduction of a thin NiCoFeCr HEA layer.
The introduced NiCoFeCr layer forms a coherent interface with the underlying HEA multilayer.
The proposed creep-testing conditions are 800°C and 100 MPa.
A coherent interface enhances atomic diffusion.
Enhanced atomic diffusion promotes a transition from diffusion-mediated creep to dislocation-mediated creep.
Adding the NiCoFeCr layer produces a 30% increase in creep resistance relative to the baseline multilayer.
The creep-resistance change can be evaluated using the steady-state creep rate in units of 10^-5 s^-1.
The baseline is an as-deposited or annealed HEA multilayer coating without the NiCoFeCr layer.
The transition between diffusion-mediated and dislocation-mediated creep occurs at a critical stress of 150 MPa.
The exact role of interface coherency in creep behavior remains unclear.
Simulation results may not fully capture the complexity of the experimental system.
Failure to observe a steady-state creep rate at least 25% higher than the baseline at 800°C and 100 MPa would falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The predicted outcome claims increased creep resistance, which ordinarily corresponds to a lower steady-state creep rate, whereas the falsification rule requires the modified multilayer to have a creep rate at least 25% higher than the baseline. The directions of improvement are inconsistent.
The proposed test is conducted at 100 MPa, but the claimed mechanism transition occurs at 150 MPa. Thus, the stated test condition does not reach the claimed critical stress.
